sections.instructions: Answer ALL questions. Unless otherwise specified, numerical answers should be either exact or correct to 3 significant figures. Working must be shown. Marks are awarded for correct method. Take π = 3.14 if a numerical answer is required. Section A (40 marks) — Answer all questions. Each question carries 4 marks.

items.prompt: [S2] Solve the inequality 3 − 2x ≥ 7.
items.solution:
3 − 2x ≥ 7
−2x ≥ 4
x ≤ −2.
(Remember to reverse the inequality when dividing by a negative number.)
items.stem: Solve the inequality 3 − 2x ≥ 7, and write down the largest integer value of x.

items.prompt: [S2] Solve the inequality 3 − 2x ≥ 7, and write down the largest integer value of x.
items.solution: The solution is x ≤ −2, so the largest integer value of x is −2.
items.stem: Solve the inequality 3 − 2x ≥ 7, and write down the largest integer value of x.

items.prompt: [S2] Make h the subject of the formula S = 2πr(r + h).
items.solution:
S = 2πr(r + h) → S/(2πr) = r + h
h = S/(2πr) − r
[or equivalently h = (S − 2πr²)/(2πr)].

items.prompt: [S2] The price of a watch is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. Find the overall percentage change in the price.
items.solution:
Take the original price as $100 (or 1 unit).
After +20%: 120; after −20%: 120 × 0.8 = 96.
Overall: a decrease of 4%.
(Successive percentage changes multiply: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96.)

items.prompt: [S2] Simplify (x² − 9) ÷ (x² + x − 12).
items.solution:
x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3); x² + x − 12 = (x + 4)(x − 3).
(x + 3)(x − 3) / [(x + 4)(x − 3)] = (x + 3)/(x + 4)
(for x ≠ 3; omitting the condition is not penalised).

items.prompt:
[S2] The straight lines AB and CD are parallel. A transversal cuts them so that a pair of alternate angles are (4x − 15)° and (2x + 35)°.
Find x.
items.solution:
Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal: 4x − 15 = 2x + 35.
2x = 50 → x = 25.
items.stem: The straight lines AB and CD are parallel. A transversal cuts them so that a pair of alternate angles are (4x − 15)° and (2x + 35)°.

items.prompt:
[S2] In △ABC, ∠A = 2x, ∠B = 3x and the exterior angle at C is 110°.
Find x.
items.solution:
The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles: 2x + 3x = 110.
x = 22.
items.stem: In △ABC, ∠A = 2x, ∠B = 3x and the exterior angle at C is 110°.

items.prompt:
[S2] A prism has a uniform triangular cross-section of area 24 cm² and perimeter 20 cm. The length of the prism is 15 cm.
(a) Find its volume, in cm³.
items.solution: V = area of cross-section × length = 24 × 15 = 360 cm³.
items.stem: A prism has a uniform triangular cross-section of area 24 cm² and perimeter 20 cm. The length of the prism is 15 cm.

items.prompt:
[S2] A prism has a uniform triangular cross-section of area 24 cm² and perimeter 20 cm. The length of the prism is 15 cm.
(b) Find its total surface area, in cm².
items.solution:
Total surface area = 2 × 24 + 20 × 15 = 48 + 300 = 348 cm².
(The two triangular ends plus the three rectangular faces, whose total width is the perimeter of the cross-section.)
items.stem: A prism has a uniform triangular cross-section of area 24 cm² and perimeter 20 cm. The length of the prism is 15 cm.

[S1] An empty rectangular tank measures 40 cm by 25 cm by 20 cm internally.
(a) Find its capacity in litres.
items.solution: Capacity = 40 × 25 × 20 = 20 000 cm³ = 20 litres.
items.stem: An empty rectangular tank measures 40 cm by 25 cm by 20 cm internally.

items.prompt:
[S2] An empty rectangular tank measures 40 cm by 25 cm by 20 cm internally.
(b) The tank contains water to a depth of 8 cm. Water is then poured in at 2.5 litres per minute for 6 minutes. Explain whether the tank overflows.
items.solution:
Water added = 2.5 × 6 = 15 L.
Water present = 40 × 25 × 8 ÷ 1000 = 8 L.
Total = 8 + 15 = 23 L.
23 L > 20 L, so the tank overflows.
items.stem: An empty rectangular tank measures 40 cm by 25 cm by 20 cm internally.

items.prompt: [S2] Two similar triangles have areas in the ratio 9 : 25. The perimeter of the smaller triangle is 24 cm. Find the perimeter of the larger triangle, in cm.
items.solution:
Area ratio 9 : 25 ⇒ side (length) ratio 3 : 5.
Perimeter of larger = 24 × 5/3 = 40 cm.

items.prompt:
[S2] The length of a rectangle is 3 cm more than twice its breadth. Its perimeter is 48 cm.
(b) Solve the equation and find the length and breadth, in cm. Give the breadth and then the length (e.g. 7, 17).
items.solution:
3b + 3 = 24 → 3b = 21, b = 7.
Breadth = 7 cm, length = 17 cm.
Check: 2(17 + 7) = 48.

(d) If both the length and the breadth are increased by 2 cm, find the percentage increase in the area, correct to 3 significant figures.
items.solution:

items.prompt:
[S2] In △ABC, AB = AC and ∠BAC = 36°. The bisector of ∠ABC meets AC at D.
(a) Find ∠ABC and ∠ACB, in degrees.
items.solution: AB = AC ⇒ base angles equal: ∠ABC = ∠ACB = (180° − 36°)/2 = 72° each.

(b) Find ∠ABD and ∠DBC, in degrees.
items.solution: BD bisects ∠ABC, so ∠ABD = ∠DBC = 72° ÷ 2 = 36° each.

(d) Hence find ∠BDC, in degrees.
items.solution: A, D, C are collinear, so ∠BDC = 180° − 108° = 72°.
items.stem: In △ABC, AB = AC and ∠BAC = 36°. The bisector of ∠ABC meets AC at D.

items.prompt:
[S2] In △ABC, AB = AC and ∠BAC = 36°. The bisector of ∠ABC meets AC at D.
(e) Show that △BDC is an isosceles triangle.
items.solution:
In △BDC: ∠DBC = 36°, ∠BCD = ∠BCA = 72°, ∠BDC = 72°.
Since ∠BCD = ∠BDC, the sides opposite them are equal: BC = BD.
∴ △BDC is isosceles.
(This is the “golden triangle”. With ∠BAC = 36° and BC = BD = AD, point D divides AC in the golden ratio.)
items.stem: In △ABC, AB = AC and ∠BAC = 36°. The bisector of ∠ABC meets AC at D.
